rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3; the authors report their own UAV multispectral flights (2017-2019) over three olive groves, visual severity surveys on each tree, polygon cokriging and discriminant analysis with cross-validation (Tables 5-8).
rows.notes: The study only classifies trees into two Xfp symptom-severity classes from UAV imagery (non-parametric cross-validation overall accuracy 0.69, early-detection class accuracy 0.77). It reports no result on controlling or limiting the spread of Xylella; the control benefit is asserted in the Introduction/Discussion as a rationale, not measured. Detection is a precondition of the claimed control effect, so upstream.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3; own UAV data acquisition, visual disease rating of every tree, geostatistical change of support and discriminant classification with cross-validation results (Tables 5-8, Figures 9-10).
rows.notes: The study monitors and classifies symptom severity and maps a canonical stress variable; it suggests in the Discussion that the maps could guide scouting and decision-making, but it does not test or report any prevention or management strategy or its outcome. Monitoring/detection is only a precondition of the claimed management effect, so upstream.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a primary detection/classification study of Xylella fastidiosa severity using UAV multispectral imagery; it contains no evidence on disease control or management outcomes, which is the function named in both claim rows.
